kiosque.name: Le kiosque à journaux · The newspaper kiosk
kiosque.alt: A green park on a sunny morning, seen from slightly above at an angle, with the bottle-green hexagonal newspaper kiosk standing right of centre under its green dome, gold finial and green-and-white striped awnings, its walls hung with magazines and its vendor at the counter. A giant golden key hangs under the awning and a small boy in red shorts reaches up and points at it. Beside the kiosk a waiter in a white apron balances a tea tray with a teapot on his head while he reads the headline of his newspaper, and at the right a magpie flies off with a glossy magazine while a man in a brown suit stares up after it with empty hands. On the kiosk steps Monsieur Verbe in a gold beret reads a big newspaper and peeks over it with a cheeky leer, and in front of him a journalist in a trench coat writes in her notebook while her little white terrier tugs at its red leash. At the left a lady in a fur hat points out the way on the park information board to a lost tourist in a sun hat, a man wearing a lemonade sandwich board sips tea on a green bench, a young lady in a new lace veil waves her newspaper over her head, and a girl in a yellow beret looks through a rolled-up magazine like a telescope. At the far left stone steps lead down to the green cellar door of the press house, at the far right a gap in the hedge leads to the cafe terrace, and the sandy path at the front right leads back to the boulevard.

doors.label: La rédaction
doors.hint: the stone steps down to the green cellar door at the far left, to the newsroom

doors.label: Les potins
doors.hint: the gap in the hedge at the far right, to the cafe terrace

potins.name: La terrasse des potins · The gossip terrace
potins.alt: A cafe terrace in the park on a bright morning, seen from the near left and slightly above, with round white tables and bentwood chairs scattered over grey paving, a long red-and-cream striped awning along the cafe front at the right, a clipped hedge at the back and sheep grazing in the sunny meadow beyond. Far back on the sandy path at the left a tall lady in red waves a long pole at a meek little man raising his bowler hat; at the back table Monsieur Verbe in a red beret chats with a woolly sheep sitting opposite him, and at another table by the hedge a second Monsieur Verbe whispers into a big brown shoe; under the awning a grandma kicks a cancan leg for her clapping friend in green. In the middle two old lady poets in purple and blue declaim back to back, a grinning moustached man in a striped waistcoat floats a teacup over his open palm, and at a table on the right a little girl shows her grandpa the big plaster with pink bows on her knee while a boy in a blue cap strikes a rapper pose, pointing at the chatterbox. In the foreground a grey-curled lady in lilac murmurs a rumour behind her lace fan into the ear of her laughing friend in a green flat cap, and at the right a man in Bavarian lederhosen chatters with both hands. At the far left the sandy path leads back across the meadow to the green domed kiosk.

doors.label: Le kiosque
doors.hint: the sandy path at the far left, back across the meadow to the kiosk

redaction.name: La salle de rédaction · The newsroom
redaction.alt: A busy newsroom under the kiosk, seen from slightly above at an angle, with bottle-green panelling, rows of wooden desks with typewriters, a big brass clock, and a black printing press at the back right with fresh newspapers flying up all around it. At the front left the editor-in-chief in a green suit and silver glasses directs the team from her desk with a big red toy duck on it, while a little girl in a toy knight's helmet stands by her chair reading out a short strip of paper. Behind them a printer lady in an apron holds up a fresh newspaper over a stack where a ginger cat sleeps, and a dad in a tweed jacket rushes past with a pile of new books, his little son running after him. At the press Monsieur Verbe in a red beret flings armfuls of papers into the air, and a reporter in a red hotel porter's uniform wheels a brass trolley of newspapers away. On the right a graduate in cap and gown waves her diploma and notebook, a red-haired reporter in a blue waistcoat holds up a huge cone with a giant pink scoop of ice cream, a man in a bull mask pins a sheet on the board, and a girl in a yellow jumper clicks a giant computer mouse with her friend. A staircase at the far left climbs up to the kiosk, a mint-green door with a bell is in the back wall, and a pale blue door is at the right end.

doors.label: Le kiosque
doors.hint: the wooden staircase and green door at the far left, up to the kiosk

standard.name: Le standard téléphonique · The switchboard
standard.alt: The switchboard room of the press house at its busiest hour, seen from the near left and slightly above: mint-green and cream tiles, round milk-glass lamps, and a huge polished wooden switchboard full of brass plugs running along the back wall, its coloured cords looping in rainbow arcs. Far back at the left a large opera singer in a red velvet gown sings with her mouth wide open, her headset rattling, while two lady operators, one beside her and one further right, signal to each other across the room with red semaphore flags; further right a young colleague presses his hands over his ears, and on the right wall a moustached man tacks a contact card onto a cork board. In the middle at the left a lady in a headset listens to her messages at a desk while her friend massages her shoulders; in the centre Monsieur Verbe in a red beret talks into a brass candlestick telephone beside a neighing brown pony; right of him an old man with white hair ponders beside a boxy answering machine, and a sailor boy pulls a rolled message out of a green bottle. In the foreground a girl in a striped poncho shoots her hand up with the answer, two grannies in cardigans chat on two chairs beside an orange traffic cone, and at the right a man in a grey suit holds a big red apple to his ear like a telephone. A bottle-green door on the left wall leads back to the newsroom; a padded walnut door at the far right leads on to the radio studio.

doors.label: La rédaction
doors.hint: the bottle-green door on the left wall

doors.label: La radio
doors.hint: the padded walnut door at the far right, under its red lamp

radio.name: Le studio de radio · The radio studio
radio.alt: The radio studio of the press house, live on air, seen from the near left and slightly above: pale walnut panels and sage-green quilted padding, a red on-air lamp, a glass window into the control room and a brass gramophone horn growing out of the wall like a flower. At the back left a lady in green turns the big round frequency dial on the wall, two tin cans dangling from its knob on a frayed string, and beside her a technician in blue overalls pushes a giant glass fuse into the broadcast panel; at the back right a man in a cardigan watches a little television set on a wooden post. In the middle a singer in a polka-dot dress freezes in a statue pose with her teacup on her break, an aunt in a red headscarf holds up all ten fingers beside a tall tripod antenna, and in the centre Monsieur Verbe in a red beret announces with one arm raised into a chrome microphone, a smiling nun beside him; at the round table the announcer in a bow tie unwraps a present, and a radio operator in a sailor cap and headphones taps his morse key. In the foreground a boy in a striped jumper dances beside a big old wooden radio set, and at the right a press photographer's flash goes off in a bright white puff. A mint-green door on the left leads back to the switchboard; a royal-blue door with gold stars at the far right leads to the debate hall.

doors.hint: the mint-green door on the left wall

debat.name: Le plateau du débat · The debate studio
debat.alt: The television debate studio of the press house, live and getting heated, seen from the near left and slightly above: royal-blue panels with gold stars, tiered wooden audience benches along the back and a giant brass boxing-ring bell hanging between two pale wooden lecterns. On the back left benches a protester in a purple jumper waves a blank placard and shouts; on the back right benches the audience laughs as a man in a checked shirt spills coffee down his front. At the left lectern a debater in a brown jacket pleads his reply, and at the right lectern a debater in a grey suit swings a cricket bat to make his point. In the middle Monsieur Verbe in a red beret scoots up on a kick scooter arguing, a lady in green points out a big blue ink mark on a man's shirt, a pundit in tweed talks into a microphone while an electric fan blows his hair back, and two lads tug opposite ends of a cord of daisies. In the foreground two women discuss on fat round cushions, and two actors read their scripts on a log. A padded walnut door on the left leads back to the radio studio; a navy double door at the far right leads to the forum.

doors.label: La radio
doors.hint: the padded walnut door on the left wall

doors.label: La conférence de presse
doors.hint: the navy double door at the far right

forum.name: La salle de presse · The press-conference hall
forum.alt: The press-conference hall of the press house, a press conference in full swing, seen from the near left and slightly above: white walls with brass sconces, a navy velvet curtain, black folding chairs scattered over a pale oak floor, and right of centre a wooden podium bristling with brass microphones, one bent over like a sunflower to listen. At the back a grey-haired lady in tweed peers through a big magnifying glass at a lamp, tapping it with her pencil; at the podium the spokesman in a navy suit reads his sheet and gives an OK sign; at the far right a speaker in a Roman toga and laurel wreath raises one arm beside a little model of Roman columns. In the middle a lady in a blue blazer cries out with a clam snapped on her finger, Monsieur Verbe in a red beret comments into his headset while combing his hair, and three men shake hands over a little table with a big pot of red sauce. In the foreground a lady in an orange jacket proudly holds up a rosette and a model mansion, and a smooth talker in a velvet jacket lounges in a red armchair, gesturing grandly. A royal-blue door with gold stars on the left leads back to the debate studio.

doors.label: Le débat
doors.hint: the royal-blue door with gold stars on the left wall

dictee.name: La salle de dictée · The dictation room
dictee.alt: The dictation classroom of the press house during the writing class, seen from the near left and slightly above: pale blue walls, round milk-glass lamps, old honey-wood desks with inkwells set at angles, and a giant quill pen standing in an inkwell taller than a man. On the low platform at the back the teacher with her hair in a bun reads the dictation from a green book, a steaming teacup in her other hand; at the blackboard on the right a boy in blue chalks a squiggle, a pot of green herbs in his hand. In the middle a girl in pigtails pulls a funny face as she rides a little red toy express train, Monsieur Verbe in a red beret corrects a big sheet with a giant red pencil beside a steaming bowl of curry, and a teacher in round glasses holds up a plate with one egg on it to show the class. In the foreground a boy in a cap salutes as he sets off on his errand with a wicker basket, a bearded grandpa in a vest lifts a huge dumbbell over his head as he recites, and a royal messenger in a blue-and-gold tabard blows a little trumpet and holds out a letter with a red seal. A bottle-green door on the left leads back to the newsroom; an oxblood-red door at the far right leads to the interview lounge.

doors.hint: the bottle-green door on the left wall

doors.label: L'interview
doors.hint: the oxblood-red door at the far right

interview.name: Le salon des interviews · The interview lounge
interview.alt: The interview lounge of the press house on interview day, seen from the near left and slightly above: rose-red brick walls, a big patterned rug, two brown leather armchairs facing each other, tall fringed standard lamps, bookcases, a framed mountain landscape painting and a potted palm wearing a tiny press badge. At the back a young candidate with braids and a folder gazes up at the mountain painting and an inventor with goggles holds up a little toy propeller to explain her idea beside the old film camera. On the left a lady in pink chooses between a straw sun hat and a yellow rain hat, and a lady in one armchair reads the newspaper with a mug of tea in each hand. In the other armchair a muddy bearded footballer with a football under his arm talks into a big microphone, and by the bookcases a man in a striped blazer makes a grand speech from a glowing disco box, holding an oar like a staff. In the middle a silly jester pulls a goofy face beside a grey seal balancing a red ball on its nose. In the front a bold young lady dashes in on roller skates, arms flung wide, and Monsieur Verbe in a red beret holds out a microphone to a little boy who waves. A pale blue door on the left leads back to the dictation classroom.

doors.label: La dictée
doors.hint: the pale blue door on the left wall
